problem: Prior VLM-based mobile manipulation systems handle only simple tasks and lack the diverse skill repertoire (rooms, floors, elevators, interactive navigation, fine base adjustment) and memory needed for very long-horizon, building-wide tasks in open-world scenes.
motivation: Service robots in homes, offices and hospitals must traverse rooms and floors, clear obstacles, use elevators and retrieve unseen objects. TAMP needs closed symbolic sets and LLMs lack visual grounding, so a VLM that unifies reasoning, perception, skills and memory could improve as backbones improve.
key_idea: Use a VLM as a central reasoner that, at each step, picks a subtask, a skill, and skill parameters from a parameterized skill library, using Set-of-Mark visual prompts with depth-derived distances, GSAM perception, and short- and long-term memory.
insight: Intermediate reasoning and grounded visual prompting matter: on OfflineSkillDataset, removing CoT drops parameter-prediction success from 80.2 to 60.7 and removing SoM drops it to 49.2. Long-term memory of past mistakes yields gains over COME (47.1 vs 35.7 average SR in real trials). Performance scales with stronger VLM backbones, and a diverse skill library lets the robot recover from sensor failures (for example using MoveBase after NaN depth).
method: Open-world perception: Grounded-SAM (GroundingDINO + SAM-HQ) segments interactable objects; depth back-projection gives object point clouds and robot-object distances.
Skill library: parameterized skills GoToLandmark (topological image map + 2D occupancy planner), NavigateNearObj, MoveBase (30 cm steps), Pickup, PushObjOnGround, OpenDoor, CallElevator, UseElevator.
Short-term memory: stores scene image, subtask, skill, parameters and detected success/failure for each step of the current trial, enabling recovery.
Long-term memory: stores human-flagged erroneous VLM predictions with context and a VLM-written failure analysis (1-3 examples per skill), collected offline and frozen during evaluation.

Two-stage decision making: first predict subtask and skill using instruction, skill descriptions, RGB, robot location, memories and SoM marks with object distances in text, with CoT; then predict skill parameters from SoM-marked candidates.
Backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as the VLM, with other VLMs (Claude, Gemini) tested on parameter prediction.

setting.training_data: none (training-free; small offline long-term memory of a few annotated failures per skill)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, 2D lidar, wrist force-torque, robot map localization
setting.action_space: parameterized high-level skills (landmark goto, move base 0.3 m, pick, push, open door, elevator buttons) executed via ROS planners and IK
setting.privileged: human-collected landmark images with pre-defined map poses for GoToLandmark; human-flagged failures for long-term memory

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 tasks (retrieve marker in B1-B3, retrieve soda can in B1-B3, rearrange chairs in B1), 10 trials each, 70 trials total
numbers.extra: long-term memory collected before evaluation; baselines extended with same skill library and short-term memory
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Success rate (%) from 10 trials in building-wide tasks; BUMBLE Avg. 47.1

numbers.eval_set_note: ~120 manually collected images with GT skill parameters
numbers.evidence: Table 2: Success Rate (%) in predicting skill parameters using OfflineSkillDataset, average 80.2

numbers_note: Per-VLM results (Claude, Gemini, GPT-4o series) and Likert user-study scores are given in figures; only the Likert 3.7 vs COME 2.6 appears in text.
results: BUMBLE achieves 47.1% average SR over 70 real-robot building-wide trials, beating COME (35.7) and Inner-Monologue (6.7, tested only in building 1). On OfflineSkillDataset it reaches 80.2% vs COME 72.6% and IM 61.7%, and the user study gives a Likert 3.7 vs 2.6 for COME.
limitations: Long-term memory grows and may become intractable; retrieval or compression is needed
GoToLandmark requires human-collected landmark images; no autonomous exploration
Frequent VLM reasoning errors in clutter (20-25 distractors) and precise localization (elevator buttons); greedy choices; skills that are hard to express in language are difficult to add
